mcqs.q: On a gingiva slide, the epithelium is:
opts: Keratinized (parakeratinized) stratified squamous with long sharp rete ridges
mcqs.explain: Gingival oral epithelium is keratinized (parakeratinized) stratified squamous with long, sharp rete ridges.

mcqs.q: The lamina propria of the gingiva is identified by its:
mcqs.explain: The gingival lamina propria is composed of dense collagen-fibre bundles, giving its firm character.

mcqs.q: The submucosa of the gingiva is:
mcqs.explain: The gingiva has no submucosa; the lamina propria attaches directly to bone, forming a mucoperiosteum.

mcqs.q: At the dento-gingival junction, the epithelium that attaches directly to the tooth is the:
mcqs.explain: The junctional epithelium (non-keratinized) attaches the gingiva to the tooth; the sulcular epithelium lines the sulcus, and the outer oral epithelium is keratinized.

mcqs.q: The hard palate epithelium on a slide is:
mcqs.explain: Like the gingiva, the hard palate is keratinized masticatory mucosa with prominent rete ridges.

mcqs.q: On the hard palate, the submucosa with ADIPOSE tissue is found in the:
mcqs.explain: The anterolateral fatty zone of the hard palate contains adipose tissue in its submucosa.

mcqs.q: The submucosa with minor salivary GLANDS in the hard palate is the:
mcqs.explain: The posterolateral glandular zone contains minor mucous salivary glands in its submucosa.

mcqs.q: Over the median raphe and rugae of the hard palate, the mucosa is:
opts: Bound directly to bone (mucoperiosteum, no submucosa)
mcqs.explain: Along the raphe and rugae, the mucosa is bound directly to bone (mucoperiosteum); a submucosa is present only in the fatty and glandular zones.

mcqs.q: The transverse ridges identified on a hard palate slide/specimen are the:
mcqs.explain: The palatine rugae are transverse ridges on the anterior hard palate, on either side of the median raphe.

mcqs.q: Which feature is SHARED by gingiva and hard palate?
opts: Keratinized epithelium and absence of submucosa over bone (mucoperiosteum)
mcqs.explain: Both are keratinized masticatory mucosa; over bone they form a mucoperiosteum (no submucosa), giving firm, inelastic attachment.

mcqs.q: The only part of the gingiva that is non-keratinized is the:
mcqs.explain: The interdental col is the only part of the gingiva covered by non-keratinized epithelium.

mcqs.q: Long, sharp rete ridges in masticatory mucosa serve to:
opts: Increase the epithelium–connective tissue interlock (resisting shear)
mcqs.explain: Long, sharp rete ridges increase the interlocking surface area between epithelium and lamina propria, helping the masticatory mucosa resist shear forces.

mcqs.q: On a slide, the gingiva is distinguished from alveolar mucosa by:
opts: Keratinization, dense collagen and absence of submucosa
mcqs.explain: Gingiva is keratinized with dense collagen and no submucosa, whereas alveolar mucosa is non-keratinized with many elastic fibres and a submucosa.

mcqs.q: The keratinization pattern of most gingival epithelium is:
mcqs.explain: Most of the gingival oral epithelium is parakeratinized (retaining shrunken nuclei in surface cells).

saqs.q: Describe the histology of the gingiva.
saqs.a: Keratinized (parakeratinized) stratified squamous epithelium with long sharp rete ridges, dense collagen lamina propria, and NO submucosa (mucoperiosteum).

saqs.q: Name the three epithelia at the dento-gingival junction.
Which part of the gingiva is non-keratinized?
How is the hard palate similar to the gingiva histologically?
saqs.a: Both are keratinized masticatory mucosa with rete ridges and form a mucoperiosteum over bone (no submucosa there).

saqs.q: Where in the hard palate is a submucosa present, and what does each zone contain?
saqs.a: Fatty zone (anterior) — adipose tissue; glandular zone (posterior) — minor mucous salivary glands.

saqs.q: Name the surface landmarks of the hard palate.
saqs.a: Incisive papilla, palatine rugae, and median raphe.
